brief: Barnabas was a Jew from Cyprus who became an apostle. He introduced Paul to the church leaders in Jerusalem. When sent to Antioch to guide the growing church there in its acceptance of Gentiles, he brought Paul into the work. The two of them took relief funds to Jerusalem and undertook a missionary journey to Cyprus and Asia Minor. Barnabas and Paul parted company at the beginning of Paul’s second missionary journey. Barnabas went to Cyprus and is regarded as the founder of the church there.
